member.name: T:Supabase.ApiKey
member.summary:
Helpers for reasoning about the format of a Supabase API key.
Supabase is migrating away from the legacy JWT-based anon / service_role keys toward opaque, non-JWT keys: publishable (sb_publishable_…, client-side) and secret (sb_secret_…, server-side). Because the new keys are not JWTs, they must travel on the apikey header only — the platform rejects them on Authorization: Bearer (except when the Bearer value exactly equals the apikey value).

member.name: F:Supabase.ApiKey.WarnedSubtypes
member.summary: Subtypes we've already warned about, so stays quiet after the first occurrence (mirrors supabase-js checkApiKeyFormat).

member.name: M:Supabase.ApiKey.IsNewApiKey(System.String)
member.summary: True when the key is a new-format opaque key (publishable or secret). These are not JWTs and must never be sent as an Authorization: Bearer token.

member.name: M:Supabase.ApiKey.CheckFormat(System.String)
member.summary: Warns (once per unrecognized subtype) when the key uses an sb_…_ prefix the SDK does not recognize. Legacy JWT keys (no sb_ prefix), the recognized new-format keys, and temporary sb_temp_ keys are all considered fine and produce no warning.

member.name: T:Supabase.SupabaseDiagnostics
member.summary:
Aggregates the diagnostic source names emitted by the Supabase clients so consumers of the meta-package can register them all with OpenTelemetry in one place, without importing each sub-package's namespace or hardcoding (case-sensitive) source names.
Each client uses the same name for its and its , so works for both TracerProviderBuilder.AddSource(...) and MeterProviderBuilder.AddMeter(...). Realtime is not yet instrumented and is therefore not included.
